title: The Science Behind the Light: Dr. Steven Vazquez on Inventing Emotional Transformation Therapy

sentences.en: Hi, I'm here with Dr. Stephen Vasquez, the inventor of emotional transformation therapy, which you can get at Taproot and lots of other places.
sentences.zh: 大家好，今天我请到了斯蒂芬·瓦斯奎兹博士，他是情绪转化疗法（ETT）的创始人，大家可以在Taproot以及许多其他地方体验到这种疗法。

sentences.en: And we're going to talk today about just kind of science and innovation and the way that he came up with that and how it works.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊聊科学与创新，以及他是如何构思出这种疗法及其运作原理的。

sentences.en: And I'll be honest, you know, when I came to ETT, it was because I had all these people
sentences.zh: 说实话，我最初接触ETT是因为当时有很多人联系我，

sentences.en: that had called me that connected with the stuff that I put out through the blog and podcaSt. I'm always looking for new models that are kind of the next thing.
sentences.zh: 他们通过我的博客和播客与我产生了共鸣。我一直在寻找那种具有前瞻性的新模式。

sentences.en: And I was very credulous, but they sounded very smart.
sentences.zh: 当时我虽然半信半疑，但他们听起来确实非常专业。

sentences.en: And I flew to Texas and Dr. Vasquez was talking about, you know, paid all this money.
sentences.zh: 于是我飞到了德克萨斯州，瓦斯奎兹博士当时正在讲课，你知道，我花了不少钱。

sentences.en: And Dr. Vasquez was talking about how color and light can heal trauma and have these effects.
sentences.zh: 瓦斯奎兹博士当时在讲色彩和光线如何治愈创伤并产生这些效果。

sentences.en: And I was just like, this is nonsense.
sentences.zh: 我当时心想，这简直是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: You know, I don't, I don't think this will work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我并不觉得这会有用。

sentences.en: And I volunteered and I could not talk myself out of it.
sentences.zh: 但我还是自愿尝试了，结果我根本无法说服自己不相信它。

sentences.en: The effects of it are immediate.
sentences.zh: 它的效果是立竿见影的。

sentences.en: And there's kind of a, you know, with, with things like the spectral chart, there's a real immediate way that it's demonstrated.
sentences.zh: 而且，通过光谱图之类的东西，这种效果有一种非常直观的展示方式。

sentences.en: So I think having read a lot more of your work now and looked at your thought process,
sentences.zh: 所以，在读了你更多著作并了解了你的思维过程之后，我认为，

sentences.en: the thing that is interesting to me about you that I think good science does is that you have big
sentences.zh: 你身上最吸引我的一点，也是优秀科学所具备的特质，就是你拥有宏大、

sentences.en: outside the box ideas, you know, that are, that are, that are new and different, but at the same time,
sentences.zh: 跳出框架的思维，这些想法既新颖又与众不同，但与此同时，

sentences.en: you have a credulousness to say, okay, you know, I thought this, it was perfectly good guess, but that was bullshit.
sentences.zh: 你又有一种坦诚，会说：“好吧，我之前是这么想的，这确实是个不错的猜测，但那纯属胡扯。”

sentences.en: It didn't work.
sentences.zh: 它没起作用。

sentences.en: And, and have a, enough skepticism to make sure that your big ideas are still like objectivity is replied to them, that they're reproducible.
sentences.zh: 而且你保持着足够的怀疑精神，确保你的宏大想法依然遵循客观性，并且是可以被复现的。

sentences.en: And I think that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这一点真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: So I mean, a lot of your work came from reading other people's research and then noticing these brain pathways.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的很多研究成果其实源于阅读他人的研究，并从中发现了这些大脑通路。

sentences.en: And I was wondering if you could tell us about some of those devices, because you, you built a couple of you talk about in the book and some of them like shining light
sentences.zh: 我很好奇你能不能给我们讲讲其中一些设备，因为你在书中提到了好几种，其中一些比如通过皮肤照射光线，

sentences.en: through skin, you discovered was kind of a dead end.
sentences.zh: 你后来发现那其实是个死胡同。

sentences.en: Like it wasn't really the, the, the way to go.
sentences.zh: 那并不是正确的方向。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But you did end up with three or four, you know, kind of really interesting devices and techniques I'd like to talk about.
sentences.zh: 但你最终确实研发出了三四种非常有趣的设备和技术，我想聊聊这些。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I, originally I was exposed to visual stimulation through syntonics optometry.
sentences.zh: 最初，我是通过综合视光学接触到视觉刺激的。

sentences.en: It's a renegade group of optometrists that use colored light to correct vision probleMs. And I noticed that when people were using that, that emotional changes would take place.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非主流的验光师群体，他们利用彩色光来矫正视力问题。我注意到当人们使用这种方法时，情绪也会发生变化。

sentences.en: And I got intrigued with how the color affected emotional states more so than correcting the vision.
sentences.zh: 比起矫正视力，我更着迷于色彩如何影响情绪状态。

sentences.en: And these were optometrists that didn't really do interpersonal work.
sentences.zh: 而且这些验光师并不真正进行人际互动治疗。

sentences.en: They just had you look at light silently 20 minutes per session.
sentences.zh: 他们只是让你静静地看着光线，每节课20分钟。

sentences.en: And of course, as a therapist, I know that the, the bond between therapists and clients is a critical factor.
sentences.zh: 当然，作为一名治疗师，我知道治疗师与来访者之间的联结是一个关键因素。

sentences.en: And so I wanted to add that into the process.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望能把这一点融入到过程中。

sentences.en: And I literally experimented, uh, people, I invited them to go through a counseling process while they looked at certain colors and I didn't, uh, know for sure what would happen.
sentences.zh: 我确实进行了实验，我邀请人们在观察特定颜色的同时进行咨询过程，我当时并不确定会发生什么。

sentences.en: Uh, and then I would have cases where dramatic changes would take place right away.
sentences.zh: 结果，有些案例中立刻就出现了戏剧性的变化。

sentences.en: In other cases where nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 而在另一些案例中则毫无反应。

sentences.en: Well, it took me a while to figure out which thing could make it happen that well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我花了一段时间才弄清楚到底是什么因素能让它产生如此好的效果。

sentences.en: Uh, one of the the first ones was the woman that had arthritic hands that were gnarled and she could, she's been in pain for 15 years and nothing.
sentences.zh: 其中第一个案例是一位患有严重关节炎、手指变形的女士，她忍受了15年的疼痛，尝试过各种方法都无效。

sentences.en: I tried looking, have her looking at different colors.
sentences.zh: 我让她尝试观察不同的颜色。

sentences.en: Nothing mattered until I got to orange and then all the pain went away.
sentences.zh: 直到看到橙色时，奇迹发生了，所有的疼痛都消失了。

sentences.en: I mean that quickly.
sentences.zh: 就是那么快。

sentences.en: So I'm thinking, whoa, there's a connection here.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，哇，这中间肯定有某种联系。

sentences.en: I want to understand that.
sentences.zh: 我想要弄明白这一点。

sentences.en: So it took me a couple of years to actually get clear on which, uh, colors did what and under what circumstances.
sentences.zh: 所以我花了几年时间才真正搞清楚哪些颜色在什么情况下会产生什么效果。

sentences.en: Uh, but I was, there are, there is technology out there for all kinds of things with light stimulation, but they don't include the interpersonal part.
sentences.zh: 不过，市面上确实有各种利用光刺激的技术，但它们都不包含人际互动的部分。

sentences.en: And in therapy, we know the research says no matter what the mental health approach is, the single factor that shows up to be the most significant is the bond between the
sentences.zh: 在治疗中，我们知道研究表明，无论采用何种心理健康方法，最显著的单一因素始终是治疗师与

sentences.en: therapist and the client.
sentences.zh: 来访者之间的联结。

sentences.en: So I needed to include that in the process, which is very different than just looking at a color.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须将其纳入流程中，这与单纯看颜色有很大不同。

sentences.en: Uh, you just look at a color.
sentences.zh: 你只是看一种颜色。

sentences.en: It may or may not be helpful, but if the person is in a state of mind that, um, that color responds to, uh, big changes can happen pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 它可能有帮助，也可能没有，但如果当事人处于某种特定的心理状态，而那种颜色恰好能与之呼应，那么巨大的改变就会很快发生。

sentences.en: That's just a little history.
sentences.zh: 这就是一点背景历史。

sentences.en: So it was, it was experimental for me.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这完全是一个实验过程。

sentences.en: I had a strong sense it would work because I would get these dramatic changes here and there.
sentences.zh: 我有一种强烈的预感它会成功，因为我时不时就能看到这些戏剧性的变化。

sentences.en: And I just had to figure out how to do that more accurately.
sentences.zh: 我只是需要弄清楚如何更精确地实现这一点。

sentences.en: And it's evolved over 25 years.
sentences.zh: 它在过去25年里不断演变。

sentences.en: And, uh, I've gone through, I think maybe seven different light devices in those 25 years, each one of them being more technologically advanced than the previous ones.
sentences.zh: 在这25年里，我大概用过七种不同的光疗设备，每一代都比前一代在技术上更先进。

sentences.en: And so, uh, that's a little bit about how that got started.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是它起步的一些情况。

sentences.en: Do you have a specific question?
sentences.zh: 你有什么具体的问题吗？

sentences.en: There's more I can say about this.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点我还有很多可以说的。

sentences.en: Well, there's, um, so there's a couple of devices that go along with ETT.
sentences.zh: 嗯，ETT配套有几种设备。

sentences.en: Um, you know, there's a spectral resonance chart, which is just a chart with extremely expensive and accurate representations of the color spectrum.
sentences.zh: 有一种光谱共振图，它只是一张包含了极其昂贵且精确的色彩光谱表现的图表。

sentences.en: Um, and then there's the light device, um, which, uh, I'll save that for the end.
sentences.zh: 然后是光疗设备，这个我留到最后再说。

sentences.en: There's the goggles, which allow, you know, light in at a different angle against the pupil.
sentences.zh: 还有护目镜，它能让光线以不同的角度射入瞳孔。

sentences.en: Um, and then there's the, the wands, which are an eye movement therapy that is similar to EMDR brain spotting, but uses color.
sentences.zh: 还有光棒，这是一种眼动疗法，类似于EMDR或脑点疗法（Brainspotting），但加入了色彩元素。

sentences.en: And then there's the light device, which kind of does all of the things because you can add in a flicker rate, you can add in a color hue, you can add, I, so it mixes sort
sentences.zh: 最后是光疗设备，它几乎涵盖了所有功能，因为你可以加入闪烁频率、调整色调，所以我说它把所有功能都融合在了一起。

sentences.en: of all of them together.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 让我和你分享一下它是如何演变的。

sentences.en: Let me share you, share with you how that evolved.
sentences.zh: 我最初其实就是从光疗设备开始的。

sentences.en: I actually started with the light device.
sentences.zh: 那是一个原始的光疗设备，只有11种颜色。

sentences.en: It's a primitive light device had 11 colors.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: That was it.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有超过1600万种颜色了，但最初就是那样开始的。

sentences.en: Uh, now we have over 16 million, but, uh, that's how it started.
sentences.zh: 后来我注意到有些人对光疗设备的刺激反应过度。

sentences.en: Uh, and then I noticed that some people got overstimulated with the light device.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说太强烈了。

sentences.en: It was too much for them.
sentences.zh: 所以我需要别的东西。

sentences.en: So I needed something else.
sentences.zh: 我曾有过一次个人经历，当时我在德国教学，有一天休息，我坐火车去参观德国那座著名的城堡，你知道，天鹅堡。

sentences.en: And I had a personal experience where I was, uh, teaching in Germany and I had one day off and I was, uh, took on train
sentences.zh: 在去那里的火车上，大约停了五站。

sentences.en: to go visit this famous castle there in Germany, you know, Swanstein on the train, on the way over there, there were about five stops.
sentences.zh: 当时我正为一段感情关系感到非常苦恼。

sentences.en: And I was at the time I was pretty upset about a relationship I was in.
sentences.zh: 在德国，每个火车站的墙壁都漆成了不同的颜色。

sentences.en: And, uh, in Germany, each train station, the walls were painted a different color.
sentences.zh: 一个车站是蓝色的。

sentences.en: One train station would be blue.
sentences.zh: 下一个是黄色的。

sentences.en: The next one would be yellow.
sentences.zh: 第三个是橙色的。

sentences.en: Third one would be orange.
sentences.zh: 当我透过窗户观察每一个车站时，我一直在处理那个困扰我的问题。

sentences.en: And as I came to look through my window at each train station, I worked on this issue that was disturbing me.
sentences.zh: 它真的起作用了，当我到达目的地时，我感到无比振奋，因为我已经释放了所有的痛苦。

sentences.en: And it worked by the time I arrived to the destination, I was exhilarated because I'd released all that distress.
sentences.zh: 所以我意识到，仅仅是观察一面彩色的墙就能达到这种效果。

sentences.en: And so I saw that looking at a colored wall could do that much.
sentences.zh: 后来我偶然发现了我们在用的那张图表，它是法国生产的。

sentences.en: And then I came across, uh, that particular chart that we use, uh, that was produced in France.
sentences.zh: 我开始使用那张图表，因为我需要一种不像直接照射眼睛那样刺激的方法，来帮助那些容易过度敏感的人。

sentences.en: And, um, I began to work with that chart because I needed something that was not as stimulating as light into the eyes for people that got overstimulated rather easy.
sentences.zh: 于是我转向了那个方向。

sentences.en: And so that's where I went to next.
sentences.zh: 这就是图表的发展过程，源于我个人的亲身体验，以及发现了这张法国生产的图表。

sentences.en: That's how the chart developed through my own personal experience with that and discovering this chart that was produced in France.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我们遇到了一些麻烦，我们买了一千张那种图表。

sentences.en: Uh, since then we've had trouble, uh, the company, we've bought a thousand of those charts.
sentences.zh: 我们把库存买断了。

sentences.en: We bought them out.
sentences.zh: 那家公司已经倒闭了，我们一直在努力寻找复制它的方法，

sentences.en: The company is no longer in action and we've been struggling to find a way to replicate it
sentences.zh: 因为那张图表非常独特，颜色极其鲜艳，达到了极致的清晰度。

sentences.en: because the chart was pretty unique and very, the colors are extremely bright, as bright as you can get, as clear as you can get.
sentences.zh: 但它只有七种颜色。

sentences.en: Uh, but there's only seven colors.
sentences.zh: 总之，事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: And, uh, anyway, so that's how that came about.
sentences.zh: 后来在与不同的人进行实验时，我注意到了一些现象。

sentences.en: And then experimenting with it, with different people, uh, I, I noticed certain things.
sentences.zh: 其中一个重大发现是，有时颜色会完全扭曲。

sentences.en: And one of the big discoveries was sometimes the color would just distort completely.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至看不见颜色，或者整张图表变成了灰色，诸如此类的情况。

sentences.en: They couldn't even see the color or else the whole chart turned gray or something like that would happen.
sentences.zh: 我最终弄明白，这是一种视觉扭曲，预示着解离状态。

sentences.en: And I finally figured out that that had to, that was, uh, um, a visual distortion that indicated dissociation.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法看到眼前的颜色，基本上说明你在心理上并不在这里。

sentences.en: Uh, if you can't see the color in front of you, basically you're not here psychologically.
sentences.zh: 所以这是识别解离最不可思议的工具之一。

sentences.en: And so this is one of the most incredible tools for identifying dissociation.
sentences.zh: 我接触的大多数看过其他治疗师的来访者其实都有解离症状，但其他治疗师并没有发现。

sentences.en: Most of the clients I get who have seen other therapists, uh, have been dissociative, but the other therapists didn't know it.
sentences.zh: 他们识别不出来。

sentences.en: They couldn't recognize it.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 解离很难捕捉。

sentences.en: It's hard to catch dissociation.
sentences.zh: 很难发现这一点。

sentences.en: It's hard to spot that one.
sentences.zh: 但这在几秒钟内就会显现出来，非常清晰。

sentences.en: This comes up in seconds and it's clear.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我们知道了这一点，就有办法去治疗它。

sentences.en: So once we know that, then there's ways to treat that anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之，这张图表在很多方面都很强大。

sentences.en: So the chart, uh, it was powerful for a number of things.
sentences.zh: 它能获取当事人意识之外的信息，并且能显示出解离状态。

sentences.en: Uh, it could access, um, information that was not conscious to the person and it could show up dissociation.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种与光刺激完全不同的工作方式。

sentences.en: So it was a, a different way to work than light stimulation.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情是护目镜，一位名叫希弗（Schiffer）的哈佛精神科医生开发了所谓的“侧向眼镜”。

sentences.en: And so what happened next was the, uh, the goggles, um, a Harvard psychiatrist named Schiffer, uh, developed, uh, what he called lateralized glasses.
sentences.zh: 他只是遮挡住光线，让你只能从左侧或右侧看到光线进入。

sentences.en: And, uh, he would just block off where you would see light coming in the left side of the eyes and then light coming in the right side.
sentences.zh: 他们是神经科学家。

sentences.en: And they were neuroscientists.
sentences.zh: 他是一位精神科医生，他们理解这一点，因为他们认为，哦，大脑右侧、左半球、右半球，他们正在产生

sentences.en: He was a psychiatrist and they understood that because they thought, oh, the right side of the brain, the left brain hemisphere, right brain hemisphere, and they were making a
sentences.zh: 治疗上的差异。

sentences.en: therapeutic difference.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本书叫《双重思维》（Of Two Minds）。

sentences.en: Uh, he, he, uh, he wrote a book called of two minds.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时疯狂地想，如果光线从12点钟方向射入，会不会比从6点钟方向更容易？

sentences.en: And so I was crazy enough to think, well, I wonder if the light came in at 12 o'clock, if that would be easier came in at six o'clock.
sentences.zh: 如果光线从各个角度射入呢？我注意到每一个角度都会带来不同的反应。

sentences.en: And if it came in all the, and I noticed that each one of them brought forth a different response.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至有一个人去他的办公室告诉他们这件事，但他们不接受，

sentences.en: And we even had a person that went to his office to tell them about it, but they wouldn't
sentences.zh: 因为他们无法用除了左右脑半球之外的任何方式来理解它。

sentences.en: accept it because they couldn't understand it any other way than the right and left brain hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现了一种通过周边眼部刺激来识别内部心理部分和生理部分的完整方法。

sentences.en: And so what we discovered was a whole way to identify internal parts, uh, internal psychological parts and physiological parts by peripheral eye stimulation.
sentences.zh: 于是我找人帮我制作了这些护目镜，它们只允许光线以特定的角度射入。

sentences.en: So I got somebody to make these goggles for me, which only allow light to come in specific angles.
sentences.zh: 这对于那些容易过度敏感的人特别有效，因为你只是让极少量的光线进入，

sentences.en: And, uh, this was particularly good for people who got overstimulated because you're just barely letting in a little bit of light,
sentences.zh: 对于患有偏头痛的人尤其有价值，因为他们对光线非常敏感。

sentences.en: particularly valuable with people with migraine headaches, particularly they had, they had a sensitivity to light.
sentences.zh: 所以这在当时是一个突破。

sentences.en: And so it was a breakthrough in that way.
sentences.zh: 我们不断发现越来越多的周边角度，它们能带来更多信息，并揭示出当事人完全意识不到的内容。

sentences.en: And we kept discovering more and more peripheral angles that did more and more and brought forth, um, information that was completely not conscious to the client.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的由来。

sentences.zh: 它需要你去感受那种感觉才能获得那种解离。

sentences.en: And so that's like, people are looking at the board and they're like, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以就像，人们看着板子，他们说，是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: This color thing.
sentences.zh: 这个颜色疗法。

sentences.en: And I'm like, we just talk about the issue.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们只是谈论这个问题。

sentences.en: And they're like, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们说，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, mom made me feel small.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，妈妈让我感到渺小。

sentences.en: And then I, I see them kind of look, cause I know they saw something, but they still don't want to know that it worked.
sentences.zh: 然后我，我看到他们看了一下，因为我知道他们看到了什么，但他们仍然不想承认它有效。

sentences.en: Like, all right, keep telling me, you know, she would always make me feel like I just didn't.
sentences.zh: 就像，好吧，继续告诉我，你知道，她总是让我觉得我只是没有。

sentences.en: And then they'll stop again.
sentences.zh: 然后他们又会停下来。

sentences.en: And they'll look and I'm like, what are you seeing in green?
sentences.zh: 他们会看，我说，你在绿色中看到了什么？

sentences.en: What are you seeing?
sentences.zh: 你在看什么？

sentences.en: Oh, I think my eyes are just doing something weird.
sentences.zh: 哦，我想我的眼睛只是在做一些奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: And it takes, you know, kind of six or seven times of them feeling that thing.
sentences.zh: 这需要，你知道，他们感受那种东西六七次。

sentences.en: And then seeing the distortion form to kind of see how it works, that it is this form of immediate biofeedback for the emotions that you cannot handle.
sentences.zh: 然后看到扭曲形成，从而了解它是如何工作的，这是一种针对你无法处理的情绪的即时生物反馈形式。

sentences.en: And that you may feel intellectually, like you're able to feel trapped or controlled or manipulated, whatever emotion you're working with.
sentences.zh: 而且你可能在理智上觉得，你能够感觉到被困住、被控制或被操纵，无论你正在处理什么情绪。

sentences.en: And these are implicit emotional states in the brainstem, not thinky, abstracted emotion, but just implicit early emotional states.
sentences.zh: 这些是脑干中的隐性情绪状态，不是思考性的、抽象的情绪，而只是隐性的早期情绪状态。

sentences.en: You know, it takes them a minute to realize like my brainstem is out of the window of tolerance there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们需要一分钟才能意识到，就像我的脑干在那里超出了耐受窗口。

sentences.en: It can't feel this.
sentences.zh: 它无法感受这个。

sentences.en: Even if I think I can feel it and I'm unaware of it, I can't feel this.
sentences.zh: 即使我认为我能感觉到它，而且我没有意识到它，我也无法感受这个。

sentences.en: And then the real work begins.
sentences.zh: 然后真正的工作就开始了。

sentences.en: And, you know, I get emails from people all over the country that, you know, say like I'm a crank because I do brain spotting or I like some of the metaphors that Carl Jung drew or
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我收到全国各地人们的电子邮件，你知道，说我是个疯子，因为我做脑部定位，或者我喜欢卡尔·荣格画的一些隐喻，或者

sentences.en: that I do, you know, ETT.
sentences.zh: 我做，你知道，ETT。

sentences.en: And so like, I shouldn't have a license because, you know, whatever, you know, they've just taken their first research 101 class.
sentences.zh: 所以就像，我不应该有执照，因为，你知道，无论如何，你知道，他们只是刚上了第一门研究101课程。

sentences.en: It's usually clinical psychology grad students that are real early on.
sentences.zh: 通常是刚开始的临床心理学研究生。

sentences.en: But like, you know, we both have seen patients that have done the more manualizable forms of therapy that randomized controlled trials like that, you know, have a place
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们都见过做过更手册化的治疗形式的患者，那些随机对照试验，你知道，有其一席之地

sentences.en: and do provide some benefit like CBT and DBT and ACT and REBT for years.
sentences.zh: 并且确实提供了一些好处，比如CBT、DBT、ACT和REBT，已经很多年了。

sentences.en: Some of these patients have been in that.
sentences.zh: 其中一些患者一直在接受这些治疗。

sentences.en: But the level of what this works on in the brain and how deep it goes, I mean, I think is a
sentences.zh: 但它在大脑中起作用的层面以及它深入的程度，我的意思是，我认为是一个

sentences.en: place that a lot of people just have a really hard time, even when they want to get better and they're
sentences.zh: 很多地方的人只是觉得很难，即使他们想好起来，而且他们

sentences.en: trying to focus on these things in like a purely relational or cognitive therapy.
sentences.zh: 试图在纯粹的关系或认知疗法中专注于这些事情。

sentences.en: And ETT and brain spotting, I mean, suck you into a different part of the brain in a different way of being with an
sentences.zh: 而ETT和脑部定位，我的意思是，把你吸入大脑的不同部分，以一种不同的方式与

sentences.en: emotional experience that are under language, you know, that are under objective thought that are
sentences.zh: 情绪体验相处，这些体验在语言之下，你知道，在客观思维之下，它们

sentences.en: more like an emotion as an energy that is just activating that now you can start to have a relationship with.
sentences.zh: 更像是一种作为能量的情绪，它只是在激活，现在你可以开始与它建立关系了。

sentences.en: And I think that's why the parts-based languages like IFS and Lifespan and, you know, voice dialogue, why they kind of meld with this pretty well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么基于部分的语言，如IFS、Lifespan和，你知道，声音对话，为什么它们与这个融合得很好。

sentences.en: And they naturally make those like a great extension of people that are already doing good work with parts-based and somatic therapy.
sentences.zh: 它们自然地使这些成为已经在做基于部分和躯体治疗的人的伟大延伸。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a repression, an avoidance defense that over time becomes automatic and all these buried emotions pile up inside a person, affect them, but the person themselves
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种压抑，一种回避防御，随着时间的推移变得自动化，所有这些被埋藏的情绪堆积在一个人的内心，影响他们，但这个人自己

sentences.en: doesn't even know where they're coming from.
sentences.zh: 甚至不知道它们来自哪里。

sentences.en: So with ETT, almost every session, people have new awarenesses.
sentences.zh: 所以使用ETT，几乎每次治疗，人们都有新的觉察。

sentences.en: The sources, the roots of their anxiety or their depression become clear.
sentences.zh: 他们焦虑或抑郁的来源、根源变得清晰起来。

sentences.en: And without that, what happens is you're going to have to fix it over and over.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这一点，发生的情况是你将不得不反复修复它。

sentences.en: But if you can get the...
sentences.zh: 但如果你能得到……

sentences.en: Or just white-knuckle it through life because you know what you're supposed to do, but the emotion is still dysregulating your behavior.
sentences.zh: 或者只是咬牙坚持过生活，因为你知道你应该做什么，但情绪仍然在失调你的行为。

sentences.en: You need to feel powerless and helpless.
sentences.zh: 你需要感到无能为力和无助。

sentences.en: And when it's not conscious, you don't have much of a shot at fixing it by yourself.
sentences.zh: 当它不是有意识的时候，你几乎没有机会自己修复它。

sentences.en: So this brings these things to conscious awareness and then we resolve them.
sentences.zh: 所以这把这些事情带到了有意识的觉察中，然后我们解决了它们。

sentences.en: That's why the depth of it affects longevity when we make a change.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它的深度影响了我们做出改变时的持久性。

sentences.en: And it's just exciting.
sentences.zh: 这真是令人兴奋。

sentences.en: As a therapist, it's exciting.
sentences.zh: 作为一名治疗师，这很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: In fact, one of my interns, she said, there's no way you could have burnout on this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我的一个实习生说，你不可能对此感到倦怠。

sentences.en: It's too exciting.
sentences.zh: 这太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You see a person make a major turnaround.
sentences.zh: 你看到一个人发生了重大的转变。

sentences.en: I mean, you're not going to get burned out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不会感到倦怠。

sentences.en: You're going to get excited.
sentences.zh: 你会感到兴奋。

sentences.en: Then her question was, what do I do with my excitement after this?
sentences.zh: 然后她的问题是，我在这之后该如何处理我的兴奋？

sentences.en: And so we share it with each other.
sentences.zh: 所以我们互相分享它。

sentences.en: And that's one way to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 这是处理它的一种方式。

sentences.en: Did you have another issue or question you want us to...
sentences.zh: 你还有其他问题或疑问想让我们……

sentences.en: Well, I'd like to be respectful of your time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想尊重你的时间。

sentences.en: This is a pretty good overview, I think, for people that are wanting to find out more about ETT or to get trained.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于那些想要了解更多关于ETT或想要接受培训的人来说，这是一个相当不错的概述。

sentences.en: Because I really do feel similar to brain spotting.
sentences.zh: 因为我真的觉得它类似于脑部定位。

sentences.en: This is just a pretty natural extension of any other effective type of therapy.
sentences.zh: 这只是任何其他有效治疗类型的非常自然的延伸。

sentences.en: That it really...
sentences.zh: 它确实……

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of times with me, I'll have talked to a patient for a long time and they're using the word angry, but that isn't really the emotion.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多时候，我会和一位患者谈了很长时间，他们一直在用“愤怒”这个词，但那并不是真正的情绪。

sentences.en: I can't really figure it out.
sentences.zh: 我真的无法弄清楚。

sentences.en: Maybe they're not able to put exactly the conceptualization around the emotion.
sentences.zh: 也许他们无法准确地围绕情绪进行概念化。

sentences.en: But we get on the board and immediately the color that goes black is what we're working with.
sentences.zh: 但我们用板子，立即变黑的颜色就是我们正在处理的。

sentences.en: And a lot of times it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 很多时候这很有道理。

sentences.en: I mean, it really helps them understand how they're really feeling, what is really coming up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它确实帮助他们理解他们真正感受到了什么，真正出现了什么。

sentences.en: And they kind of immediately are like, oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎立即就会说，哦，好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, I wasn't allowed to feel angry.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不被允许感到愤怒。

sentences.en: So I was calling this, you know, I was calling this like something else.
sentences.zh: 所以我把这个，你知道，我把这个称为其他东西。

sentences.en: But really, that's what it is, is I don't feel like I can have a voice.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这就是它，我感觉不到我能有发言权。

sentences.en: And, you know, a lot of that is just so interesting and so helpful for therapists that are curious and really want to
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，其中很多内容对于那些充满好奇心、真心希望

sentences.en: always be prepared to handle the next thing that they don't know how to handle.
sentences.zh: 时刻准备好应对下一个未知难题的治疗师来说，既非常有趣又非常有帮助。

sentences.en: You know, there's a lot of tools here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里有很多工具。

sentences.en: Do you have anything to kind of cap us out that is helpful that you kind of would like to say to providers that may have questions or be interested about how to find out about ETT?
sentences.zh: 你有什么想对那些可能有疑问或对如何了解 ETT 感兴趣的从业者说的，作为我们这次谈话的总结吗？

sentences.en: Oh, sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, we have a website that has all the trainings coming up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们的网站上有所有即将开展的培训信息。

sentences.en: We do them.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在举办这些培训。

sentences.en: We've got about 10 people that are trained to be facilitators for ETT.
sentences.zh: 我们大约有 10 位受过培训的 ETT 引导师。

sentences.en: And I mainly do them here in Austin, Texas, where I am.
sentences.zh: 我主要是在我所在的德克萨斯州奥斯汀进行培训。

sentences.en: And we have people around the country that train there's even one of them in Europe that will do trainings from there.
sentences.zh: 我们在全国各地都有培训人员，甚至在欧洲也有一位，他们会在当地进行培训。

sentences.en: So it's available on our website.
sentences.zh: 所以这些信息在我们的网站上都能找到。

sentences.en: Do I need to give that address?
sentences.zh: 我需要提供那个网址吗？

sentences.en: I can put all that in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我可以把所有这些信息都放在节目说明里。

sentences.en: And so anybody can click the link if they're on the YouTube or if they're on the podcast, you'll see that link to the ETT training beneath.
sentences.zh: 这样任何人，无论是在 YouTube 上还是在播客上，都可以点击链接，你会在下方看到 ETT 培训的链接。

sentences.en: So you can find out more about the model and then also register for a training if you'd like to.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以了解更多关于该模型的信息，如果愿意的话，还可以注册参加培训。

sentences.en: Particularly brain spotting and EMDR providers.
sentences.zh: 特别是对于那些从事脑部定位（Brainspotting）和眼动脱敏再加工（EMDR）的从业者。

sentences.en: I mean, I think this kind of continues to enhance what you're doing and it would probably be a good extension of those.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这能进一步提升你们现有的工作，而且它很可能是这些疗法的良好延伸。

sentences.en: There's never been a study that actually compare them, but I get therapists all the time who have
sentences.zh: 虽然从未有过真正对比它们的研究，但我经常遇到一些治疗师，他们

sentences.en: been doing EMDR particularly, and then they no longer do that after they get EMDr. So that happens repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 之前主要是做 EMDR 的，但在学习了 ETT 之后就不再做 EMDR 了。这种情况反复发生。

sentences.en: So that's their perspective on it, but they haven't actually done an actual study on it, but I'm open to that if and when that would ever take place.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们的个人看法，虽然还没有进行过实际的研究，但如果未来有相关研究，我持开放态度。

sentences.en: So it's taught, there's seven courses.
sentences.zh: 课程设置方面，总共有七门课程。

sentences.en: Let me explain.
sentences.zh: 让我解释一下。

sentences.en: The first course covers two methods, the multidimensional eye movement and the use of the spectral chart.
sentences.zh: 第一门课程涵盖两种方法：多维眼动和光谱图的使用。

sentences.en: The second course involves the light device as well.
sentences.zh: 第二门课程还涉及光疗设备的使用。

sentences.en: And gosh,
sentences.zh: 天哪，

sentences.en: I'm always going blank here in the second course.
sentences.zh: 我总是记不起第二门课程的内容。

sentences.en: The light device and the goggles, okay, the peripheral eye stimulation.
sentences.zh: 是光疗设备和护目镜，对，还有周边视觉刺激。

sentences.en: The third course has specific applications to the most common psychological challenges, depression, anxiety, trauma, OCD.
sentences.zh: 第三门课程针对最常见的心理挑战有具体的应用，比如抑郁、焦虑、创伤和强迫症。

sentences.en: So it covers a variety of things, but it's mostly trauma focused and you become certified as a ETT, complex trauma therapist after that.
sentences.zh: 所以它涵盖了多种问题，但主要侧重于创伤，学完后你可以获得 ETT 复杂创伤治疗师的认证。

sentences.en: The fourth one focuses on somatic issues like physical pain, stress-related illness, sleep disorders, things of that nature on the fourth course.
sentences.zh: 第四门课程侧重于躯体问题，如身体疼痛、压力相关疾病、睡眠障碍等这类问题。

sentences.en: The fifth course is the spiritual and religious issues.
sentences.zh: 第五门课程是关于精神和宗教问题的。

sentences.en: And a lot of people have those kinds of issues.
sentences.zh: 很多人都有这类困扰。

sentences.en: The sixth course is on addictions.
sentences.zh: 第六门课程是关于成瘾问题的。

sentences.en: So number six is addiction.
sentences.zh: 所以第六门是成瘾治疗。

sentences.en: The seventh course is on couple therapy, how you apply this to couple therapy.
sentences.zh: 第七门课程是关于伴侣治疗的，即如何将此方法应用于伴侣治疗中。

sentences.en: So those are the seven basic courses we teach applications for ETT.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们教授 ETT 应用的七门基础课程。

sentences.en: So anyway, that's some information I think people need to have.
sentences.zh: 总之，我认为这些信息是大家需要了解的。

sentences.en: I do, I start in January with level one and we go through the whole year all seven by the time we get to the finish, but there's other people in other parts
sentences.zh: 我会在一月份开始第一阶段的培训，然后贯穿全年，到年底完成全部七门课程，但也有其他人在其他地区

sentences.en: of the country that are teaching it at different points.
sentences.zh: 在不同的时间点进行教学。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: We'll link to all of that.
sentences.zh: 我们会把所有相关链接都放上去。

sentences.en: And if you have any interest, please go to the website, find out some more about ETT.
sentences.zh: 如果你有兴趣，请访问我们的网站，了解更多关于 ETT 的信息。

sentences.en: I do think it's a pretty natural extension of what a lot of good providers are already doing and just gives you some more tools in your toolbox.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是许多优秀从业者现有工作的自然延伸，它只是为你提供了更多的工具。

sentences.en: So thank you so much for talking with us and we look forward to talking with you again.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你接受我们的采访，我们期待再次与你交流。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
